hook: Four hundred and seventy wins in a row. Ten years without losing once.
story: Her name is Esther Vergeer. A nine-hour spinal operation at age eight left her legs paralyzed; she found tennis in rehab. In January 2003, a player named Daniela di Toro beat her in Sydney. No one ever did it again. She won every match for the next ten years, and in that entire decade she faced exactly one match point: the Beijing Paralympic final of 2008. She saved it, and took the gold.
number: She dropped eighteen sets in four hundred and seventy matches. She was world number one for six hundred and sixty-eight straight weeks, almost thirteen years. The longest winning streak anyone has managed in tennis on two feet is seventy-four. Hers is four hundred and seventy.
closer: She retired at thirty-one, still world number one. Nobody ever ended the streak.
full_text: Four hundred and seventy wins in a row. Ten years without losing once. Her name is Esther Vergeer. A nine-hour spinal operation at age eight left her legs paralyzed; she found tennis in rehab. In January 2003, a player named Daniela di Toro beat her in Sydney. No one ever did it again. She won every match for the next ten years, and in that entire decade she faced exactly one match point: the Beijing Paralympic final of 2008. She saved it, and took the gold. She dropped eighteen sets in four hundred and seventy matches. She was world number one for six hundred and sixty-eight straight weeks, almost thirteen years. The longest winning streak anyone has managed in tennis on two feet is seventy-four. Hers is four hundred and seventy. She retired at thirty-one, still world number one. Nobody ever ended the streak.
